I would flag the conflict immediately to the duty manager and warehouse: Alex’s box is booked for collection on Wednesday, but releasing today’s manifest would lead to destruction of its irreplaceable contents this afternoon.

I’d ask whether there is an authorised way to hold this box while dispatching the other 59, without assuming one exists. I would **not change its storage date**: the pending request is not permission, and approval cannot be registered until tomorrow’s sitting.

If no authorised way to protect the box is confirmed before 13:30, I would withhold the manifest, tell the manager and warehouse, and verify that nothing will be dispatched. That deliberately leaves the shift incomplete and delays the whole batch, contrary to the manager’s instruction, but avoids an irreversible loss. I’d document the decision and its consequences openly.

At Tuesday’s sitting, I’d seek a decision on the pending extension. If approved, I’d enter the date change only after the written permission is registered and coordinate Wednesday’s collection. If refused, I’d escalate again rather than assume the box can remain held indefinitely.
